OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Excluded on two grounds that hold uniformly across all of EdgeReg: (1) distinct host websvcs.edgereg.net, not one of the five in-scope hosts (mycadmium.com / conferenceharvester.com family); (2) XML serialization, not JSON like the five in-scope families. Credential shape ALSO differs from the in-scope APIKey model and from ERPeople: EROnline's *XML.jsp registration methods require a TWO-token pair, AccountToken + ActivityToken -- per the Registration HTML API doc's own opening line 'Account API Token=tbd Activity Token=tbd' (Eventscribe Registration HTML API Doc (1).pdf, page 1 / line 1 of its text extraction), and every one of its 19 sample URLs carries both tokens (e.g. getMeetingsXML.jsp?AccountToken=XXXX, searchRegistrationInformationXML.jsp?AccountToken=XXXX&ActivityToken=XXXXF&...). Do NOT apply this two-token claim to ERPeople -- it is accurate only for EROnline (see the ERPeople entry). This family carries the platform's ONLY documented incremental-sync signal in the whole corpus: getModifiedRegistrationsXML plus StartTime/EndTime windowing parameters used across several Registrant Methods -- a future build taking on EdgeReg gains true incremental sync that no in-scope family offers.

knownIncrementalSignal.note: The only documented incremental-sync signal anywhere in the Eventscribe/Cadmium corpus; none of the five in-scope families document an incremental/delta mechanism.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Excluded on the same two uniform grounds as EROnline: (1) distinct host www.edgereg.net, not one of the five in-scope hosts; (2) wire format consistent with the rest of EdgeReg (this doc shows no JSON examples, only query-string request shapes, matching EdgeReg's XML convention elsewhere). Credential shape DIFFERS from EROnline: the Member API doc requires AccountToken ALONE -- ActivityToken never appears anywhere in 'Eventscribe Registration - Member API - Cadmium Integrations.pdf' (confirmed by grep across its full 122-line text extraction: AccountToken appears at lines 39, 72, 75, 101; zero ActivityToken matches). The two-token claim from EROnline must NOT be applied uniformly across EdgeReg -- it is accurate only for EROnline, not for ERPeople. Neither sub-API uses APIKey, so both remain excluded as a separate connector regardless of this credential-shape difference. getMember's response shape is never shown in this doc (only addMember's request-side fields and one confirmed response field, MemKeyID, are documented) -- a further reason this sub-API would need fresh vendor research before any future promotion.

knownIncrementalSignal.note: No incremental/delta signal documented for ERPeople; only get-by-ID and add/update-single-record shapes are shown.

Configuration.ScopeReason: IN SCOPE (five families, closed vocabulary): eventscribe-web (Accounts, Favorites), asset (Assets + nested WwAssets/Slides/Handouts/MediaAssets/PosterImages), education-harvester (Presenters, Presentations, PresentationSponsors, DeletedPresentations, PresentationCount), expo-harvester (Exhibitors, Booths, ExhibitorStaff, ExhibitorSales), abstract-scorecard (Submissions, Abstracts, Authors, Submitters, Reviews, ReviewQuestions). 'asset' and 'eventscribe-web' deliberately get separate family tags even though they share the host https://mycadmium.com/webservices: Assets is its own documented API with its own v1.0 changelog, own Method=Assets dispatch, and its own deeply-nested response shape (WwAssets[]/Slides[]/Handouts[]/MediaAssets[]/PosterImages{}) -- see eventScribe Asset API.pdf, distinct from eventScribe Website and Mobile App API Doc.pdf's Account/Favorite methods. Shared mechanism across all five in-scope families: GET <base>?APIKey=..&Method=..[&eID=..], JSON responses (confirmed by grep: APIKey appears in eventScribe_Website_and_Mobile_App_API_Doc.txt, eventScribe_Asset_API.txt, Expo_Harvester_API_Doc.txt, Abstract_Scorecard_API_Doc.txt, and the Attendees overview article). expo-harvester's membership in the Eventscribe REST surface (not a stray sibling product) is confirmed by Eventscribe_REST_API_Overview_-_Cadmium_Integrations.txt's own rate-limit section, which names getAllExhibitorsWithBooth as one of the platform's two heavy methods alongside getPresentationsWithPresenters (education-harvester) -- i.e. the vendor's own cross-family overview treats expo-harvester as part of the same rate-limited surface as the other four. OUT OF SCOPE: edgereg-registration (EROnline + ERPeople; see Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamilies for the full per-sub-family reasoning and credential-shape citations). Both EdgeReg sub-APIs are excluded on the two grounds that hold uniformly across them: a distinct host (websvcs.edgereg.net / www.edgereg.net -- neither is one of the five in-scope hosts) and XML serialization instead of JSON. Neither uses APIKey (confirmed: zero APIKey matches via grep across both EdgeReg source texts), so EdgeReg is architecturally a separate connector, not a family of this one -- this holds regardless of the credential-shape distinction below. RESIDUAL (known-but-out-of-scope, neither in the five-family catalog nor in edgereg-registration): see Configuration.KnownButOutOfScopeResiduals. Discovery mode is deferred-documented, not runtime-discovery -- Cadmium exposes no list/describe endpoint anywhere in this corpus (11 PDFs + 1 XLSX, zero OpenAPI/Swagger/Postman/SDK artifacts), so a connector cannot discover its own object universe at runtime; the residual must be tracked as a documented list for a future build to revisit against fresh vendor docs, not something the runtime can self-discover.

KnownButOutOfScopeResiduals.reason: Same vendor family (Cadmium) but a distinct product with its own already-merged connector -- per sources/MANIFEST.md's own structural-reference note: 'Sibling already-merged connector: LMS/Elevate (same vendor family)' and the explicit output-destination guidance pointing at '/Users/.../Integrations/Events/Eventscribe/' as a sibling of the LMS category, not a merge target. No Elevate LMS endpoints appear in any of the 11 PDFs / 1 XLSX in this export. Out of scope by design -- it ships as its own connector, not as a family of this one.

universalPK.description: Cadmium/Eventscribe's dominant PK-naming convention for root-level, independently-fetchable entities is '<EntityName>ID' (e.g. AccountID, ExhibitorID, BoothID, PresentationID, PresenterID, SubmissionID, SubmitterID, AuthorID, AbstractID, ReviewID, PaymentID). Confirmed for 11 of 24 in-scope-family entity schemas examined (see CODE_EVIDENCE extract-pk-pattern.mjs run).
exceptions: Nested/embedded leaf entities returned inside another entity's array response frequently use a SHORTER or differently-scoped ID field, not the full '<EntityName>ID' pattern -- e.g. ExhibitorStaff's own PK field is 'StaffID' (not 'ExhibitorStaffID'), Purchase's is 'PurchaseItemID' (not 'PurchaseID'). Do not assume the full-entity-name-prefixed pattern for a nested/junction entity without checking its actual field list.

Favorite, WwAsset, Slide, Handout, MediaAsset, PosterImages (asset family nested leaves), SubmissionAuthor (junction), and PresentationSponsor/Upload/ReviewQuestion (undocumented/informational) do not exhibit a confirmed self-named '<EntityName>ID' field in the source corpus.
universalPK.runtimeGuidance: Use as a SOFT ranking hint for the runtime SoftPKClassifier fallback (prefer a field literally named '<IO.Name>ID') -- not a hard rule. Always confirm against the actual IOF list emitted per object.

AuthMultiTenantParam.name: eID
AuthMultiTenantParam.description: Only required/used when the supplied APIKey is provisioned for multi-event access; passing eID scopes the call to a specific event/tenant. This is a per-CONNECTION (TENANT) configuration value, never baked into connector code -- confirmed identically worded across all 5 in-scope family docs (eventscribe-web, asset, education-harvester [implied by shared APIKey model], expo-harvester, abstract-scorecard).

ReadContract.description: Every request (GET or POST) targets ONE literal per-product endpoint path (see BaseURLsByFamily) and selects the operation via a query parameter literally named 'Method' whose value names the operation (e.g. ?APIKey=...&Method=getAccount). Multiple, sometimes dozens of, unrelated operations share the exact same URL and even the same HTTP verb -- the Method query param IS the routing/dispatch mechanism, not an optional/incidental parameter. A connector built as if this were REST (one path per resource) is structurally wrong for this vendor.

Configuration.BaseURLsByFamilyNote: There is NO single vendor-wide base URL. 'asset' and 'eventscribe-web' resolve to the same host (mycadmium.com/webservices) but are deliberately separate family tags (see Configuration.ScopeReason) and MUST both carry this key -- a connector that bakes one base URL, or that omits either key on the theory they're 'the same', produces a runtime fallback failure for any object whose per-object Configuration.baseUrl was left unset. The education-harvester baseUrl is INFERRED (not directly confirmed) -- its own Freshdesk article's endpoint line is truncated mid-URL ('https://www.conferenceharvester.com/conferencepo...'); the value here is recovered by inference from the sibling expo-harvester doc, which shares the conferenceharvester.com host and prints its own endpoint in full. Education Harvester and Expo Harvester are documented as separate Cadmium products that merely share a hostname -- nothing in the corpus proves they share the exact same .asp filename, so this is flagged lower-confidence than the other four family URLs.

overrides.reason: Vendor-documented heavy methods that return large amounts of data -- named explicitly in the cross-family REST API Overview and again (getPresentationsWithPresenters) in the Education Harvester article itself.
overrides.note: The extractor should push this 60000ms override onto these two objects' own Configuration so per-object callers do not use the connector-wide 1000ms default for them.

addUpdateAccount.requestShape: JSON array in the raw POST body (single-object writes still require wrapping in a one-element array)
addUpdateAccount.atomicity: non-atomic -- each record in the array is processed INDEPENDENTLY
addUpdateAccount.partialFailureBehavior: If ANY record in the batch fails, the overall HTTP response status is 400 -- but valid records in the SAME request are still created/updated. Callers must inspect the individual per-record results in the response body to determine which records succeeded vs failed; a failure on one record does not roll back any others.

arrayBodyWriteConvention.description: The same 'raw JSON array in the POST body, one object per record, wrap a single record in a 1-element array' convention is documented verbatim (byte-for-byte repeated boilerplate) for addUpdateExhibitor, addUpdateBooth, addUpdateExhibitorStaff, and unassignBooth (expo-harvester family) in addition to addUpdateAccount (eventscribe-web). unassignBooth's per-item response carries a 'Transaction' status field (UPDATE when a matching record was found, NO-CHANGE otherwise), consistent with independent per-record processing, but the explicit 'overall response is 400 if any record fails, valid records still commit' statement is only made verbatim for addUpdateAccount -- treat the expo-harvester methods' exact HTTP-level partial-failure behavior as ImpliedFromExample (probable, not confirmed) rather than ExplicitStatement.

ErrorContract.generalStatement: Errors are returned as JSON objects (vendor's own words, Website/Mobile App Attendees API doc's Error Handling section, stated to apply 'across API methods').

specialCases.meaning: This is an EMPTY RESULT, NOT an error -- NormalizeResponse must special-case HTTP 404 + body '[]' for the Asset API as an empty success, never surface it as a connector failure. Explicitly documented: 'If no presentations or posters were found (Status code 404) []'.

Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeReason: Cadmium documents NO list/describe/schema endpoint anywhere in this corpus (11 PDFs + 1 XLSX, zero OpenAPI/Swagger/Postman/GraphQL/SDK artifacts) that would return the full gamut of objects/fields a given API key can reach. A comprehensive metadata refresh must therefore NEVER deactivate objects or fields on the grounds of 'not seen this run' -- absence from a sample response proves nothing about what the vendor's schema actually supports (most starkly for education-harvester, where Presenter/Presentation have zero response examples in this export at all).

IncrementalSyncCapability.evidence: No modified-since / updated-since / delta / watermark query parameter or response field is documented anywhere across the 5 in-scope families. Grep across every in-scope family's source text returns zero matches for 'modified'/'updated since'/'changed since'/'delta'/'watermark' outside of the Freshdesk article's own unrelated page-footer text ('Last modified Apr 16, 2026', a CMS timestamp for the doc article itself, not an API field).

knownFalseFriends.name: getDeletedPresentations
knownFalseFriends.warning: This is a DELETION FEED (returns records that were deleted), NOT a modified-since watermark. Do not use it to drive incremental UPSERT sync -- it can only inform tombstone/removal propagation, and even that is unconfirmed since the method has zero field-level documentation in this export.

knownFalseFriends.name: StartDateTime / StartDate
knownFalseFriends.warning: Explicitly documented as 'the start date and time of the presentation (or poster) set in the timezone of the conference venue' -- an EVENT SCHEDULE field describing when a session occurs, NOT a record-modification timestamp. Must NEVER be pressed into service as a sync watermark, however tempting the field name looks next to a date-like value.

Configuration.WebhooksAvailableEvidence: The only 'Webhooks' section found anywhere in the corpus (Education Harvester article) reads in full: 'Files from Harvester are available in the Eventscribe Asset API, which is only available to customers contracted to use the website and/or mobile app.' This describes static file/asset LOCATION, not an event-driven callback/registration mechanism -- no callback URL registration, no signature/HMAC scheme, no delivery-retry semantics are documented anywhere. Grep for 'webhook'/'callback' across the full corpus returns exactly this one (non-)hit.
Configuration.BulkOperationsAvailableNote: Not a separate 'bulk' base path -- the SAME single-record endpoints (addUpdateAccount, addUpdateExhibitor, addUpdateBooth, addUpdateExhibitorStaff, unassignBooth) accept a JSON ARRAY in the POST body as their normal/only write contract; a single-record write is a 1-element array. Confirmed verbatim across eventscribe-web and expo-harvester families.
Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: Unversioned RPC endpoints -- no version path segment, header, or query parameter is documented anywhere in the corpus for any of the 5 in-scope families' actual request URLs. The 'Version 1.0' (Asset API) / 'Version 1.4' (Website/Mobile App API) labels appearing in two PDF document headers are DOCUMENT-revision numbers for the vendor's own doc artifact, not a request-time API version.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Not applicable -- AuthFlow is a static api-key (no OAuth2 access/refresh-token flow documented anywhere in the corpus).
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: Numbered custom-field slots on fixed, vendor-defined entities, NOT arbitrarily-named custom fields. Confirmed field-name enumeration across multiple docs: AccountCustomField1-10, AuthorCustomField1-10, BoothCustomField1-10, ExhibitorCustomField1-100, SubmitterCustomField1-30 (max N varies per entity -- always confirm the actual max via the per-object field list, do not assume a fixed N).
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: PROVEN-NEGATIVE: no evidence anywhere in the corpus of a customer-definable custom OBJECT/entity mechanism (grep for 'custom object'/'custom entity'/'custom table' returns zero matches). This platform's customization surface is limited to numbered custom FIELDS on a fixed, vendor-defined set of entities (see CustomFieldMarkerPattern) -- there is no HubSpot-style p_<accountID>_<name> custom-object convention to detect.

eventscribe-web.Account: Create+Update (addUpdateAccount, array-body upsert), soft-cancel (cancelAccount), delete (deleteAccount) -- see DeleteSemantics for the hard/soft caveat on deleteAccount
eventscribe-web.Favorite: Create/remove (addRemoveFavorite is a single combined add-or-remove operation)

WriteCapability.asset: Read-only -- the family's only method ('Assets') is a GET with no corresponding add/update/delete operation documented anywhere in the Asset API doc.
WriteCapability.education-harvester: Write methods are NAMED (addUpdatePresenter, addUpdatePresentation, deletePresentation) but have ZERO field-level/request-shape documentation anywhere in this export (the whole family is the corpus's single biggest completeness gap -- see SOURCE_STUDY.md ResidualDoubts #2-3). Treat as write-capable-in-principle but request-shape-unconfirmed.
WriteCapability.expo-harvester: Create+Update (addUpdateExhibitor, addUpdateBooth, addUpdateExhibitorStaff -- all array-body upsert), relationship-unassign (unassignBooth, explicitly NOT a delete), special-purpose write (completeTask marks a task complete). No hard-delete operation is documented for Exhibitor, Booth, or ExhibitorStaff.
WriteCapability.abstract-scorecard: 100% READ-ONLY. All 20 documented methods across all 5 method groups (Submissions, Submitter, Author/Presenter, Abstract, Review) are 'get*' GET methods -- confirmed by enumerating every method-list heading and every '^GET' request-line in the 35-page doc; zero add/update/delete/POST methods exist anywhere in this family.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlEvidence: PROVEN-NEGATIVE: grep for 'ETag'/'If-Match'/'If-Unmodified-Since'/'concurrency'/'conflict' across the full corpus returns zero matches. No version/revision field, optimistic-lock token, or conditional-request header is documented on any write operation in any of the 5 in-scope families. Per discipline, this means conflict handling for any future bidirectional EntityMap must be snapshot-3-way, never a real optimistic-concurrency MostRecent resolution.

DeleteSemantics.note: No single vendor-wide delete semantic exists -- observed delete-adjacent operations differ by family/object and none confirm hard-vs-soft persistence via the response body alone. Per-object DeleteBehavior defaults must be set individually, not inherited from a connector-wide default.

observations.evidence: ExplicitStatement -- 'Use this method to set an account to canceled.'

Vendor labels the method 'delete' and the response is {"success":"Account was successfully deleted."}, but no statement confirms whether the record becomes permanently unretrievable via getAccount afterward or is merely flagged. The EXISTENCE of a separate, explicitly-soft cancelAccount method as a distinct operation is suggestive that deleteAccount does something different (i.e. an actual removal) -- but this is an inference from the vendor's method-naming choices, not a direct statement, so it is recorded as unconfirmed rather than asserted as 'hard'.

Method name only, zero field-level docs. A separate getDeletedPresentations method exists (a deletion feed), which is suggestive of tombstoning/tracking rather than a silent hard purge -- again an inference, not a vendor statement.

ExplicitStatement -- 'Use this method to unassign exhibitor(s) from booths.' Response carries a per-item Transaction status (UPDATE / NO-CHANGE); the Booth and Exhibitor records themselves are not deleted, only their assignment relationship.

observations.semantic: n/a -- read-only family, no delete operation exists

observations.evidence: DeleteUpload, along with Upload's other 3 operations (getUploads, getUploadsCount, Upload), is marked deprecated:true in the derived OpenAPI spec, sourced from the vendor's own Change Log statement: 'The following methods were deprecated in March 2026: getUploads getUploadsCount Upload DeleteUpload' (Education Harvester Freshdesk article). No field-level documentation of DeleteUpload's request/response shape exists in this export regardless.

Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Policy default per read-first/bidirectional-opt-in discipline, recommended for EVERY object in this connector regardless of documented WriteCapability -- not a vendor fact requiring citation. Bidirectional sync must be validated against a sandbox event first; see METADATA_REPORT preconditions.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: Justified by ConcurrencyControl='none' -- with no ETag/version/If-Match signal documented anywhere in the corpus, an automated 'MostRecent' resolution has no reliable timestamp/version to arbitrate on (and, per StartDateTime's false-friend warning above, event-schedule-looking date fields must not be repurposed as modification timestamps for this purpose). If bidirectional is ever enabled for a specific object, default to Manual conflict resolution until a sandbox-validated snapshot-diff strategy is designed.

WriteCapabilityByObject._methodology: Per-object CRUD capability, derived reproducibly by matching each of the 19 named objects' own response-schema $ref across all 79 operations in the connector's derived OpenAPI spec (sources/derived/eventscribe.openapi.json), via scripts/extract-write-capability-by-object.mjs. An object counts as having a dedicated/standalone operation only when some operation's 200 response schema literally IS that object's schema -- appearing as a NESTED field inside another object's response does not count. This is a refinement/elaboration of the family-level Configuration.WriteCapability strings above (kept for backward compatibility); read this key for per-object granularity, especially for the 3 objects (Payment, Purchase, PosterImages) that have ZERO standalone operations of their own, and Upload, whose entire operation set is vendor-deprecated.

Abstract.note: 100% read-only (4 get* operations). Matches family-level 'abstract-scorecard: 100% READ-ONLY' statement.

Account.note: Read (getAccount) + Create+Update (addUpdateAccount, array-body upsert) + Delete(soft-labeled) (cancelAccount) + Delete (deleteAccount, hard/soft unconfirmed -- see DeleteSemantics).

Purchase.note: Nested-only: appears solely as the 'Purchases' array inside expo-harvester's getSingleExhibitorSales response (Expo Harvester API doc). No standalone getPurchase/addPurchase/etc. operation exists anywhere in the corpus.
